**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 103, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):**

(p-87) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah al-'Asr (The Time)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾.

Al-'asr is a noun for all of time or for a part of it.

For this reason, its intended meaning has been disputed, since it is not clarified here.

It has been said: it is the whole of time (al-dahr). Allah swore by it because of what it contains of wonders: a nation passes and another comes, a decree is carried out, a sign appears, and it itself does not change. Night follows day and day drives away night, so it is in itself a wonder.

As it has been said:

It exists, resembling the non-existent, and it moves, resembling the still.

As it has been said:

*"I see time as a ship sailing with us toward death, and we do not see its movements."*

So it is in itself a sign, whether in its past, where one does not know when it began, or in its present, where one does not know how it passes, or in its future.

This view is supported by what has been transmitted as a statement attributed to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and as a transmission traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) from an irregular reading (qira'a shadhdha): "By time and the calamities of the age." It is taken as an interpretation if it is not established as Qur'an. This meaning is also related from Ibn Abbas.

On this is the verse of the poet:

*"The path of desire is rugged, and the sea of desire is deep; a day of desire is a month, and a month of desire is an age."*

It has also been said that al-'asr is the night and the day.

(p-88) Humayd ibn Thawr said:

*"The two 'asr periods did not delay a day and a night when they sought to reach what they would complete."*

Al-'asran also means the morning and the evening.

As it has been said:

*"I delay him through the two 'asr periods until he tires of me, and he accepts half the debt while the nose is still rubbed in the dust."*

Al-matl means procrastination and delaying a debt.

As it has been said:

*"Every debtor has paid and fulfilled his creditor, but the one who is delayed in its payment has been made to suffer."*

It has also been said that al-'ashiyy is the period after the sun has passed its zenith until its setting. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatada.

From this is the verse of the poet:

*"Let us go out in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short, and in the first afternoon journey is the spoil and the reward."*

Qatada also said: it is the last hour of the day, for the glorification of the oath by it, and because Allah swears by the dawn and the forenoon.

It has been said: it is the 'Asr prayer, because it is the middle prayer.

It has been said: it is the era of the Prophet (ﷺ) or the lifetime of his community, because it resembles the 'asr (late afternoon) of the life of this world.

What appears to be the case, and Allah knows best, is that the closest of all these views are two: either the general meaning of time (al-dahr), in accordance with the irregular reading, since its lowest level is that of an interpretation, and because its generality includes the rest of the views;

or the 'asr of the human being, that is, his lifespan and the period of his life, which is the place of gain and loss, as the context suggests, and because it particularly concerns the servant himself as an admonition and a benefit.

This second meaning is supported by what surrounds this surah: the preceding surah of at-Takathur (Competition for Worldly Gain) and the following surah of al-Humazah (The Backbiter). The first condemns this preoccupation and the competition in wealth and children, even to the point of visiting graves at death, and the place of all this is the life of the human being.

(p-89) The surah of al-Humazah, in essentially the same meaning, says: ﴿He who gathers wealth and counts it,﴾ ﴿thinking that his wealth will make him immortal.﴾ [al-Humazah: 2-3]

So gathering wealth and counting it occurs in the life of the human being, and his life is limited; it is not everlasting in this world. Likewise, faith and righteous deeds are linked to the life of the human being.

In light of this, the intended meaning of al-'asr in this surah may be generality, since it includes everyone and accords with the irregular reading, and this is the strongest of the views.

Or it may be the life of the human being, since it is most closely bound to him in his action, and all the other usages would be of the type of the whole with the intention of a part. Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾

The word "mankind," though singular in form, has the definite article (al) which makes it generic.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and him, clarified this in order to remove the appearance of inconsistency, and the note on this has been mentioned repeatedly before. So it includes the Muslim and the disbeliever, except those whom Allah excepts.

It has been said: it is specific to the disbeliever, but the first view is preferred because of its generality.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ is the answer to the oath. Al-khusr (loss) has been said to mean deception in a bargain, or deficiency, or punishment, or ruin. All of these are close in meaning.

The root of khusr and khusran is like kufr and kufran: a deficiency in the capital. The kind of loss and what it is in is not specified here; rather, it is stated in general terms so as to encompass everything. The particle of place (fi, "in") is used to indicate that the human being is immersed in loss, and it surrounds him from every direction.

If we consider two matters, namely the exception and the surah preceding it, this generality becomes clear. The implication of the exception covers four things: lack of faith, which is disbelief; lack of righteous deeds, which is corrupt action; lack of mutual enjoining of truth, which is either the complete absence of mutual enjoining or enjoining falsehood; and lack of mutual enjoining of patience, which is either the complete absence of mutual enjoining or anxiety and impatience.

And the surah preceding it describes the human being's distraction with competition in wealth and children, seeking riches and increase in them. Its opposite is the loss of wealth and children, which is khusran.

(p-90) Accordingly, loss in religion occurs in terms of faith because of disbelief, and in Islam, which is the abandonment of action, even though faith in the technical sense includes it. It also occurs in distraction with falsehood and abandonment of the truth, and in anxiety and fear.

From this also comes the abandonment of commanding good and forbidding evil, in what contains the servant's benefit, success, and the righteousness of his religion and his worldly life. All of this is found in the Qur'an, and we summarize the evidence for it as follows:

As for loss through disbelief, it is as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers.﴾ [az-Zumar: 65]

And His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost,﴾ meaning: because they did not work for this meeting, and they neglected their affairs in the life of this world, so they lost themselves and their share in the Hereafter.

As for loss through abandoning action, it is as in His saying: ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 9], because the scales are the measures of deeds, as has been explained earlier: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.﴾ [az-Zalzalah: 7]

Similar to it is: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾ [an-Nisa': 119], because he will be among the party of Satan: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 19], meaning by obeying them in disobedience to Allah.

As for loss through abandoning the mutual enjoining of truth, there is nothing after the truth except error, and the truth is Islam in its entirety. He, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be in the Hereafter among the losers.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 85]

As for loss through abandoning the mutual enjoining of patience and falling into anxiety and fear, it is as He, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on the edge; if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss.﴾ [al-Hajj: 11]

* * *

**Tahqiq al-Manat** (verification of the ground of the ruling, i.e., examining the actual reality) on the true nature of human loss

They agree that the capital of a human being in his life is his lifespan. He is charged with employing it during his existence in this world, which is for him like a marketplace. If he employs it in good, he profits; if he employs it in evil, he suffers loss.

(p-91) This meaning is indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise﴾ [at-Tawbah: 111], to the end of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [as-Saff: 10-11], to the end of the verse.

In the hadith in Muslim: "Purity is half of faith."

And at its end: "Every person goes out in the morning, and either he sells himself and frees it, or he destroys it." This confirms that the capital of a human being is his lifespan.

Because of the importance of this lifespan, it is paired with the mission and the warning in His saying: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? And the warner came to you.﴾ [Fatir: 37]

On this basis they have said: Allah, may He be exalted, sent His Messenger with guidance, and He guided every person to the two paths (an-najdayn), and He made for every person a station in Paradise and a station in the Fire.

Whoever believes and does righteous deeds, his destination is the station of Paradise, and he is safe from the station of the Fire. Whoever disbelieves, his destination is the station of the Fire, and he forfeits his station in Paradise.

As in the hadith of the grave: "When a believer enters his grave first, a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'That is your seat in the Fire had you not believed.' Then it is closed, and a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This is your station, until the Hour arises.' He then says: 'My Lord, establish the Hour!'"

If he is a disbeliever, it is entirely the opposite. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, each takes his station. The stations of the people of the Fire in Paradise remain empty, and the people of Paradise inherit them. The stations of the people of Paradise in the Fire remain empty, and they are distributed among the people of the Fire. Here the manifest loss becomes apparent, because whoever leaves a station in Paradise and goes to a station in the Fire is without doubt a loser. And if he leaves his station in Paradise for another and takes instead the station of another in the Fire, that is the manifest loss, we seek refuge with Allah.

As for someone other than a disbeliever, and for the general body of Muslims, the loss lies in negligence, such that if he enters Paradise but does not attain the highest ranks, he feels the loss at the time he was negligent, and he did not compete in doing good so as to attain the highest ranks.

(p-92) Therefore this surah is indeed a driving force for every individual toward diligence and profitable action. The ranks of Paradise are lofty, and its stations are high, however much effort the servant exerts, for before him is room for gain and profit. We ask Allah for success and prosperity.

They have said: No person leaves this world except in sorrow. If he was an evildoer, then it is over his evil; and if he was a good doer, then it is over his shortcoming. This meaning may be supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30]

So fear of the future is before them, and grief over the past is behind them. Allah knows best.

What makes the gravity of this matter clear is that when a person is at the end of his life and feels the nearness of his limited days and his counted hours, and wishes to add a day in which he could provide for himself, or a brief hour in which he could make up for some of what he missed, he finds no way to do so. Then he feels regret and sorrow over the days, nights, months, and years that were wasted on him without any gain or benefit, which could have been profitable for him. In the authentic hadith: "Two blessings are ones in which many people are deceived: health and free time."

That is: they pass by, and he does not use them in the complete forms of gain, so they are lost to him without any compensation worth mentioning. Then he regrets, but it is too late for regret.

As has been said about this:

*"Gray-haired and bald has replaced my thick locks, and pearls have replaced my bright teeth, as the Muslim buys when he becomes Christian."*

* * *

**Note**

In Surah at-Takathur there is a condemnation of being distracted by competition in wealth and children and the like, and then an indication that its cause is ignorance, for if they had known with certain knowledge, that distraction would not have diverted them until death overtook them.

Here too there is an indication that the cause of this loss into which a human being falls is ignorance, which (p-93) leads to disbelief and persistence in falsehood. Hardness of heart and long hope help this. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth, and not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the time became long for them, so their hearts hardened? And many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hadid: 16]

**Another note**

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾: it specifies mankind, as explained above. Yet another verse shows that jinn are like mankind in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect among nations that had passed before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 18]

The explanation of the jinn's obligation to the call, their response to it, and their calling others to it has been given earlier.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) [Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book]:

(p-465) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah al-'Asr

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 103, verse 1 (part 2 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse indicates that the one of whom it is reported that he is in loss is a single human being, as evidenced by the singular form of the word "al-insan" (mankind/the human being), and by the exception made from that single human being in the wording.

His saying: ﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr: 3] requires that it is not a single human being.

The answer to this is: the word "al-insan," although singular in form, takes on the sense of a general category through the definite article "al-" (alif and lam) which denotes comprehensiveness (al-istighraq). By means of these two, the singular noun becomes a form of generality. Accordingly, the meaning of "inna al-insan" is that every human being is included, due to the indication of the comprehensive "al" upon that.

And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 103, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to the truth, and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

This is the exception from the preceding "man" (mankind), which indicates generality, as we have already mentioned. Iman (faith) linguistically means tasdiq (affirmation, assent), and in the Shari'ah it means the firm conviction in the six pillars of faith (arkan al-iman), as in the hadith of Jibril, peace be upon him, with the Messenger ﷺ when he asked him about Islam, iman, and ihsan.

"And do righteous deeds": the conjunction (al-atf) requires difference.

For this reason some people said that deeds are not included in the definition of faith, and their statements are well known.

The majority hold that faith is conviction in the heart, utterance with the tongue, and action with the limbs.

So action is included in it, and it increases and decreases. We have already mentioned that action is a condition, closer to being a part; that is, faith is true by conviction and its existence does not depend on action, but action is a condition for benefiting from faith, when the servant is able to act. Among what indicates that faith is true by the definition of conviction and utterance even when the servant is unable to act is the story of the Companion who embraced Islam at the start of the battle, fought, was martyred, and never performed a single rak'ah for Allah, and he entered Paradise.

The majority also hold that mere conviction does not benefit its holder, as the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ believed in the truth of his message, but he did not utter a word by which he could argue on his behalf ﷺ. Likewise, if one believes and utters the two testimonies but does not act, he contradicts his own words.

(p-94) We have already discussed this issue in detail.

As for "righteous" (al-salihat), it is the plural of salihah. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, had already defined it, and the conditions for an deed being righteous are established by their evidences: that it conforms to the Book of Allah, that its doer performs it sincerely for the sake of Allah, and that it proceeds from a believer in Allah, etc.

His saying: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾.

Enjoining one another to the truth is considered a specific matter after a general one, since it is included in doing righteous deeds.

It has been said: enjoining one another means that some of them advise others to the truth.

It has also been said: the truth is everything that is the opposite of falsehood, so it includes performing acts of obedience and abandoning sins.

He considered this a foundation of the principles of enjoining good and forbidding evil, by the indication of the pairing with "enjoin one another to patience," i.e., regarding commanding and forbidding, as will come, Allah willing.

It has been said: the truth is the Qur'an, because it encompasses every command, every prohibition, and all good. The evidence for this is His saying concerning the Qur'an: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾ [al-Isra: 105].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [az-Zumar: 2].

Its verses in the Qur'an indicate that the enjoining of the truth includes the entire Shari'ah, its roots and branches, its past and present. Among this is what Allah enjoined upon the prophets, and in general, from Nuh, Ibrahim, and those after them, in His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein﴾ [ash-Shura: 13].

Establishing the religion means upholding it in its entirety. This enjoining was the work of the messengers for their nations and those after them. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, carried it out, as Allah said: ﴿And Ibrahim enjoined it upon his sons, and Ya'qub: "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132].

After Ibrahim came Ya'qub, as Allah said: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133].

(p-95) Thus is the enjoining of nations regarding the root of faith and the generality of the Shari'ah, and likewise regarding worship, such as prayer and zakah, as in His saying about the prophet of Allah, Isa, peace be upon him: ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾ ﴿and dutiful to my mother﴾ [Maryam: 31-32].

Likewise, the social condition is evident in the enjoining regarding parents and children, for the bond of the family. Regarding parents, He said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man regarding his parents: his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years — "Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination." ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, and accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 14-15].

Regarding children, He said: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [an-Nisa: 11].

Regarding general rights, there are commands and prohibitions, acts of worship and dealings, and the verses of the Ten Commandments came, about which Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whoever wishes to look at the will of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon which is his seal, let him recite: ﴿Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited for you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and do not kill your children out of poverty — We provide for you and for them — and do not approach immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This He has instructed you that you may reason﴾ ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge a soul except [according to] its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it is [to one of] near kin. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This He has instructed you that you may remember﴾ ﴿And indeed, this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has instructed you that you may fear Him﴾ [al-An'am: 151-153].

These are the comprehensive instructions that open the doors of good, close the doors of evil, and are concluded with this clarification and definition: ﴿And indeed, this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways﴾.

If we wished to connect this with "enjoining one another to the truth," and both with al-Fatihah, the result would be as follows: in His saying ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾, it refers to those instructions, which are comprehensive and all-encompassing, and are titled as being the straight path of Allah.

(p-96) So His saying ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ is equivalent to: "and enjoin one another to the straight path, and remain steadfast upon it."

Then in Surah al-Fatihah: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6], and this is the path of Allah, the straight one, so follow it.

Thus Surah al-Asr includes the enjoining of steadfastness upon the straight path of Allah and following it. Following it is His saying: ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ [al-Asr: 3], serving as the reinforcement of this straight path, since patience is necessary for performing acts of obedience, just as it is necessary for abstaining from what is forbidden.

These ten instructions combined commanding and forbidding, doing and abstaining. Similarly, they contain an indication of what the callers to Islam say: that righteous deeds, calling to the truth, and enjoining it upon one another involve commanding good and forbidding evil, and whoever undertakes this often encounters the harm of people, so enjoining one another to patience becomes necessary, as Luqman said to his son, advising him and combining in his counsel the counsel of Surah al-Asr when he said: ﴿O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is good, forbid what is wrong, and bear patiently what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Luqman: 17].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, had already explained the rules of commanding good and forbidding evil in detail at His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves. Whoever strays cannot harm you if you are [rightly] guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], in Surah al-Ma'idah.

Thus this surah has truly become comprehensive of the foundations of the message.

As has been narrated from al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "If people were to reflect upon this surah, it would suffice them."

His saying: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾. The exhortation to enjoin one another to mercy has also come alongside patience, in His saying: ﴿Then he was of those who believed and enjoined one another to patience and enjoined one another to compassion﴾ [al-Balad: 17].

With these three instructions: enjoining one another to the truth, enjoining one another to patience, and enjoining one another to compassion, the components of the complete society are perfected, whose foundation is the best virtues and the most excellent values.

Because enjoining one another to the truth establishes the truth and steadfastness upon the straight way.

(p-97) And by enjoining one another to patience, they are able to continue their journey upon this path and overcome every obstacle that confronts them.

And by enjoining one another to compassion, they become bound together like one body. These are gifts that none has given except the Qur'an, and it has given them in this concise surah. And success is from Allah.

Note (tanbih)

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: When Allah, exalted is He, informed about these people of their salvation from loss, and their success through righteous deeds and faith, He informed about them that they did not limit themselves to what concerned their own souls, but went beyond to others, calling them to what they had attained, in line with His saying ﷺ: "Love for your brother what you love for yourself." End of quote, summarized.

This is witnessed by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them﴾ up to His saying ﴿And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾ ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between you and him is hostility [will become] as though he were a devoted friend﴾ ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 30-35].

Allah has thus made clear that people are of three categories in the face of the call of the messengers:

A people who believed, said "Our Lord is Allah," and remained steadfast upon that through righteous deeds.

A people whose resolve rose to calling others, and they are without doubt the best in speech.

And a people who opposed the callers and harmed them.

Then He clarified the stance of the callers toward those who harm them within His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil]﴾, i.e., repel the harm of the wrongdoers with what is better, so that they become your allies, and He clarified that this station ﴿is not granted except to those who are patient﴾, and then that whoever rises to it and follows its path is indeed one of great fortune.

(p-98) Note (tanbih)

I had heard from the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, his saying to the callers that there are two enemies: one from mankind, and the other from the devils.

Allah has guided us to how to overcome both of them and to avert their evil.

As for the enmity of mankind, it is by repaying evil with good, so that the enemy becomes a devoted friend.

As for the enemy from the jinn, it is by seeking refuge in Allah from him: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 36].

We ask Allah for guidance and success.

We have already pointed out that the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, presented the topic of enjoining good and forbidding evil at His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves. Whoever strays cannot harm you if you are [rightly] guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105].

He mentioned Surah al-Asr there and laid out several issues regarding the methodology of enjoining good and forbidding evil, to a degree that is indispensable.
